title: Confiscation of vehicle in excise cases - how to get it released
p1:
Your vehicle can be seized in an excise case — but does that mean you lose it forever?

Many people assume that once police confiscate a vehicle, there is no way back. That belief can create unnecessary stress for vehicle owners.
p2:
The surprising fact is that confiscation is not always the final step. In many cases, the owner can seek release of the vehicle by approaching the proper authority and showing that continued custody is not justified.

The law generally focuses on facts like ownership, involvement of the vehicle, and compliance with legal procedures.
p3:
A common mistake is waiting too long after seizure. Quick legal action, proper documents proving ownership, and a clear explanation of the vehicle’s role in the case can significantly affect the outcome.

The key takeaway: seizure and confiscation are not the same. Seizure is taking possession temporarily, while confiscation is a further legal action that requires due process.
